newsitem.title: INDIA: India soybean sowing starts as monsoon rains begin.
newsitem.headline: India soybean sowing starts as monsoon rains begin.

text.p: Sowing for the 1997/98 (Nov-Oct) soybean crop has started in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh, after the area received its first monsoon showers, traders said on Tuesday.

"Satisfactory rains started in central India and farmers have made elaborate arrangements to plant soybean in a big way," said an oilmeal broker in the central city of Indore, the hub of India's soybean industry.
Madhya Pradesh contributes 80 percent of India's soybean output.
Traders said farmers received higher prices for their produce in the 1996/97 season which would tempt them to increase the area planted to soybeans in 1997/98.
The Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA), in its preliminary estimates, set a soybean production target of 5.9 million tonnes in 1997/98 compared with four million in the current season.
SOPA expects the area under soybean cultivation to increase to 5.7 million hectares from five million in 1996/97.
Meteorological officials said on Tuesday monsoon rains had covered most parts of Madhya Pradesh.
Soybean arrivals in central Indian markets were about 700 tonnes per day, compared to about 1,500 tonnes at the same time last year, traders said.

Soybean was quoted at 11,500 to 11,800 rupees per tonne compared with 12,000 to 12,900 last week. Traders said Indian soymeal export prices eased about $15 to $16 per tonne during the week on sluggish export demand. Soymeal for export was quoted at $268-270 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship).
Export prices for rapeseed extraction fell by about $8-$9 per tonne during the week to $107-$108 FAS, they said.
